## papers 3.0.0b5

Fixes found while using 3.0.0b4, and:

- Undo in a shallow library takes the pool along. A command that writes
  the library and its pool (`add` in a shallow library, auto-push, `push`,
  `sync`) records the pool's step with its own. `papers undo` and
  `papers redo` in the library undo and redo that step in the pool too,
  when the pool is still where the command left it; the PDF that `add`
  moved to the pool goes back where it came from. If the pool changed
  since, its step is reverted there instead (a new step of the pool), and
  redo reverts that revert. `--library-only` leaves the pool as it is.
  With auto-push, undo and redo push the entries that differ from the pool
  afterwards, as any command does (in general there is nothing to push).
- `papers history --revert N` takes back step N alone, as a new step, and
  keeps the steps made after it (`papers undo -n N` goes back over the
  last N steps). Per entry: what step N changed goes back, unless it
  changed since (a conflict, `--on-duplicate` as in `pull`); tags and file
  links one by one; the files of step N go back as undo moves them.
- A lock: a command that changes a library holds `.papers/lock` (refreshed
  every 2 seconds; stale after 10 seconds, or at once if its process is
  gone), so that two commands, or papers and another program, do not write
  the same library or pool at the same time. Another command waits, says
  which command holds it, and stops after 30 seconds. Commands that only
  read do not wait.
- In the history of a pool, a step made from a library names it
  (`from ~/papers/paper2`).
- `papers history` shows the size of the files each step keeps, and
  `papers history --drop-files N|PATH` removes from the history the files
  that step N deleted, or the file deleted from PATH (to the trash of the
  system; undo no longer brings them back).

Fixes:

- A redo that deleted a file again recorded a step of its own
  (`papers redo`) and moved the library onto it.

- `papers file clean` in a shallow library cleaned the folder of its
  `filesdir` setting, which a shallow library does not use (it can be the
  folder of another library): it is now refused, and says to clean the pool
  (`papers -C POOL file clean`), where all the entries that link to the
  files are known.
- The files that a command deletes without changing the bibtex (`papers
  file clean`), and the file operations of a command stopped by an error or
  Ctrl-C, are a step of the history: `papers undo` brings the files back.
  Before, they were kept in the history but no step referred to them.
- Ctrl-C ends papers without a traceback (exit code 130).
- The question of `papers file clean` reads `[y: yes, n: no, Y: all, N: none]`.
